items.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01
items.q: On saxophone we had Omar Simeon.

ctx.x: Yes, we talked to him up and he's in Baton Rouge. We saw him last January. Last January.

Well we went with King Oliver. Let's see, I think I can remember some of the names in that band. It was pretty long ways back. But on trumpet there, they had King Oliver. They had a trumpet player called Gray. So far I can't remember his name. He was Gray and Red Allen. It was three trumpets. On trombone we had one, we had Kid Ory on trombone. Now on bass we had a fellow, but his name was Buford. That's all I can remember. Buford, heavy dog. Buford, he was a bass player. On saxophone we had Omar Simeon. I think…
Just a week and a half ago.

items.title: Omer Simeon Interview, 1955-08-18
items.q: On the alto sax. The three joined us in St. Louis.

ctx.x: On the alto sax. The three joined us in St. Louis. And from there we went to New York. We stayed around New York, what, a month, a couple of months or so. Played an engagement at the Savoy for two weeks. Then, after we finished the Savoy, Joe didn't have a very good booking agent. So it was really a struggle then, keeping the band together. And they started leaving, one by one, coming back to Chicago. I think Clarence Black was the first one to leave. Then Kidd Ory, and eventually Bonnie and I left. Then we…
Was he still playing pretty well then?

items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1971-03-13
items.q: Simeon. Oh, Omar. Omar Simeon. Yeah, that was our read section.

ctx.x: Great kind of guy. Darnell Harris?

No. No, Darnell Harris, in fact Darnell Harris taken his place. Oh really? In Chicago. And you knew him too. Yeah, he went away to Paris, France with Wilbur. Oh, I love that. Wilbur to Paris. Simeon. Oh, Omar. Omar Simeon. Yeah, that was our read section. Well we had a good band and so I won't get off that, but the band broke up because we were supposed to go in the cotton club and King Oliver wanted too much money, so instead the band got Duke Ellington. And that's why King Oliver made his mistake, because his…
I see. That's how you got up with Jell-A. Yeah, that's how I got up with Jell-A-Roll-Martin. Because King Oliver's band broke up.
